title: Relative clauses with que and quien: adding information

sections.content: You know relative clauses with *que* and *quien* from B1 Unit 5. *Que* links a noun with a clause about it, for people and for things. *Quien* is used for people, usually after a comma. They let you add information without starting a new sentence, which is useful for the commission, the president and the people of the Guatemalan war.

items.spanish: Árbenz fue el presidente que hizo una reforma agraria.
items.english: Árbenz was the president who carried out a land reform.

items.spanish: La CEH, que presentó su informe el 25 de febrero de 1999, contó más de 200.000 muertos o desaparecidos.
items.english: The CEH, which presented its report on 25 February 1999, counted more than 200,000 dead or disappeared people.

items.spanish: Rigoberta Menchú, quien pertenece al pueblo maya, recibió el Premio Nobel de la Paz en 1992.
items.english: Rigoberta Menchú, who belongs to the Maya people, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1992.

items.spanish: El altiplano es una zona que tiene muchas aldeas mayas.
items.english: The highlands are an area that has many Maya villages.

sections.content: Never drop *que*: Spanish needs it where English can say "the president I mentioned". Do not add a second pronoun: *el presidente que hizo la reforma*, not *el presidente que él hizo la reforma*. After a comma with a person, *que* and *quien* are both possible.
